ClariDi · model-design experiments

Four ways to condition the same latent bridge model

Ours, a stock-VQ-GAN baseline, and three conditioning variants (specimen label, A: stained references, B: unstained context), trained and tested on the same spatially blocked 5-fold split.

Images throughout: tile A_row7_col1_10x10 (specimen A, brain), held out in fold 0; VS = draw 0. Reconstructions in panel A are real outputs of the fine-tuned and the stock VQ-GAN.

1 / 7
Method

Ours: stain-aware VQ-GAN + latent Brownian bridge

  • (A) Stage 1. The pretrained VQ-GAN is fine-tuned on C&SF images, so its latent space captures stain-specific structure.
  • (B) Stage 2. The VQ-GAN is frozen and a Latent Brownian Bridge Diffusion Model is trained from scratch to map UA latents to C&SF latents.
  • Inference. Encode UA, run 200 reverse bridge steps starting from y = E(UA), decode with the frozen decoder.
  • Objective (same for every variant): xt = (1−mt)x0 + mt y + √δt ε; the UNet εθ(xt, t, c) regresses mt(y − x0) + √δt ε. Here c = 0.

Needs at test time: the UA tile only.

Shared by all five runs: 50 epochs · batch 8 × 4 accumulation · Adam, lr 10−4 · T = 1000 · EMA 0.995 · same spatial folds.

2 / 7
Baseline

Vanilla L-BBDM: stock ImageNet VQ-GAN

  • Stage 1 is skipped. Encoder and decoder keep the ImageNet weights; nothing is tuned on tissue.
  • Stage 2 is unchanged. Same L-BBDM, objective, schedule, sampler and folds; c = 0.
  • Isolates what stain-aware latent tuning contributes.
  • Panel A shows the stock VQ-GAN's own reconstruction of the C&SF tile.

Needs at test time: the UA tile only.

3 / 7
Variant 1

+ specimen label (oracle): one learned vector per specimen

  • c = W[s]: a learned 512-d embedding per specimen (11 specimens + a null label), added to the UNet's timestep embedding.
  • Learns a per-specimen bias, such as colour balance and stain intensity, from that specimen's training tiles.
  • 10% null-label dropout in training, as in classifier-free guidance training; sampled without guidance.
  • Standard class conditioning (Dhariwal & Nichol 2021). 6,144 extra parameters.

Needs at test time: the specimen's identity, and that specimen must have been seen in training: an oracle-identity ablation that does not transfer to a new specimen.

4 / 7
Variant 2 · A

+ A (extra input): statistics of stained reference tiles

  • Each reference tile is encoded by the frozen VQ-GAN and summarised by its per-channel latent mean and std (512-d); these are averaged over k references and mapped by an MLP to c.
  • References: C&SF tiles of the same specimen from that fold's training split, never from the tile's own crop unit. k = 8 random in training, all of them at test.
  • Last MLP layer zero-initialised (training starts as ours); learned null, 10% dropout; about 0.53M extra parameters.
  • Pooled mean and std carry colour and intensity more than texture.

Needs at test time: stained (C&SF) tissue of the same specimen, so this is a few-shot, extra-input setting.

5 / 7
Variant 3 · B

+ B: the same, from unstained context tiles

  • Identical to A, except the statistics are computed on the UA inputs of the specimen's training tiles.
  • Tells the model what this specimen looks like before staining, not what its stain should be.
  • Same MLP, k, dropout and null; about 0.53M extra parameters.
  • In these runs the bank holds the specimen's training tiles, so the comparison with A is like for like.

Needs at test time: UA tiles of the same specimen, which always exist, so B is the form of specimen context that could be deployed on a new specimen.

Same split, schedule and sampler for all five; only the encoder (vanilla) or c (the three variants) changes. Ours and vanilla are plain image-to-image translation. The label is an oracle that does not exist for a new specimen. A needs stained tissue from the same specimen, so it must be presented as a few-shot or extra-input setting. B needs only uncleared tissue, which is always available.
